renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: We want to see the deep place and live in its cave. We bow to those who see the moon-crowned Lord even in dreams, for he gives the best joy.

We want to think hard about what he is like, and that wish cuts the fear of being born again. We promise to keep our minds on him alone all our lives. We bow to him as the tree that grows holy books and grants wishes. We give him all we say and do so we can become like him, free of either-or. No one else has his free power over making and unmaking. His bare name beats all other props. Every road and word and quiet thought ends in him.

renders.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms.

paragraphs.text: We want to see the deep and move into its cave. Shoutout to the ones who catch the moon-crowned Lord in dreams -- pure bliss dealer.

We crave to brood on what he is, and that craving snaps rebirth-fear. Single-pointed on him for life, for real. He is the book-tree and the wish-tree in one. We hand over speech, mind, body, goings -- made of him now, no more versus. Nobody else runs making and unmaking for free. His name alone outranks every other crutch. Every path, word, sit still ends at him.
